newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo cen.bank to convert credits into securities.
newsitem.headline: Yugo cen.bank to convert credits into securities.

text.p: The Yugoslav central bank plans to offer credit relief both to the state and the country's commercial banks by converting all credits given to them into securities, a central bank official said on Friday.
"The central bank Board of Governors decided to convert all credits given to the Yugoslav state at the beginning of 1994 into state bonds," the central bank vice-governor Ratko Banovic told Reuters.
"Credits given to public companies will also be converted into bonds, while commercial banks' borrowing will be exchanged for honoured drafts without any limits," Banovic said.

The whole operation is expected to take place by the end of 1996. Banovic would not reveal the value of credits to be converted into securities. He did not expect those securities to attract a substantial investor interest to begin with.
"But despite the expected low demand at first, we would at least have clear signals as to which banks and companies enjoy investor trust," Banovic said.
"The initial demand would serve to create the first internal rating of Yugoslav banks and companies," he added. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
